extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, PRSA members, and the interested public (historical record)
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions of the Public Relations Society of America (PRSA) professional accreditation program: its purpose, structure (two-part exam), administration (written under testing firm supervision; oral by accredited examiners), and eligibility standards (experience, character, reputation). Historical notice of 430 executives accredited and posted following PRSA's annual meeting (1965).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the accreditation program
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The purpose of the accreditation program is to raise the professional standards of public relations and to recognize those who have demonstrated a high level of competence in the public relations field.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement attributed to Kalman B. Druck, chairman of the accreditation board; frames accreditation as both a standards-raising and recognition mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation program development and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society's accreditation program has been developed over a three-year period, and comprises a two-part examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the program's multi-year development and that accreditation depends on passing both parts of the examination (written + oral).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written examination administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The written examination is given under the supervision of a professional testing firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies external professional supervision for the written component; implies standardized, professionally administered testing procedures (no scoring details provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral examination format
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral examinations are conducted by a three-man team of examiners, all of whom are themselves accredited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes peer evaluation by a small accredited panel for the oral component; implies examiner qualifications (must be accredited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility and approval standards
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for accreditation must pass the two examinations and, also meet other rigid standards of experience, character and reputation before the Accreditation board approves and grants PRSA accreditation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond exam performance, approval requires meeting unspecified but described-as-rigid standards of experience, character and reputation; final approval rests with the Accreditation board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting / recognition of accredited individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society posted the names of 430 public relations executives who have been accredited under the Society's professional accreditation program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditation confers public recognition; initial list was presented at PRSA's annual meeting in New York (Nov. 19, 1965).
